annotations.text:
PALScans — six design directions, three pages each.
A and B follow the familiar dark-violet manga-site layout (marked ASURA-STYLE). C–F are deliberate alternatives.
Same content in every direction so they compare fairly. Pick one direction, or mix: e.g. home from B, series from A, reader from F.
Ad slots are drawn as dashed boxes at final size; footer carries Discord + socials. Covers are placeholders.
Series page for 'Return of the Frost Monarch' in all six directions. Same stats, chapters and actions everywhere.
Reader on a phone (390×844) — where reading actually happens. One ad after the last page, never between pages. Chrome shown visible; it hides on tap.

A · Violet Classic (ASURA-STYLE)
The layout your readers already know: carousel hero, updates grid, popular sidebar. Familiar and dense.
Tradeoff: looks like the rest of the category.

B · Violet Refined (ASURA-STYLE)
Same information architecture, calmer execution: one featured card, a card grid, hairlines and glass.
Tradeoff: less content above the fold than A.

C · Editorial Noir
Magazine treatment: one featured story, oversized numerals, whitespace. The most distinctive.
Tradeoff: fewer titles per screen; needs strong art direction to stay fresh.

D · Catalog Grid
Search and filters are the hero. Maximum density, mono numerals. Best for a big catalog and power users.
Tradeoff: no curation on the front page; the least emotive.

E · Daylight
The light theme, proven end to end including the reader. Friendly, broad appeal.
Tradeoff: dark is the category norm; many readers will toggle.

F · Cinematic Rows
Streaming-app feel: full-bleed hero, horizontal rails, glass chrome. Strong on phones and big screens.
Tradeoff: rails hide depth; harder to scan forty updates at once.
